source: Green Fire Research and Innovation Center — Council, Creativity & Community Solutions
excluded: Commercial media offerings (packages, cinematic, studio, workshops, pricing, booking) are deliberately not part of the OS. This is the civic and ecological doctrine only.
operating_sentence: People listen to one another and to the land; organize at the scale of watersheds and ecosystems; make transparent, reversible decisions; build useful projects; teach what they learn; circulate value locally; measure real effects; and adapt together.
double_mandate: What does this living place require or permit?

core_commitments.name: Dual intake
core_commitments.detail: Human needs are heard through community listening, while ecological conditions are understood through observation, mapping, data, and seasonal indicators.

core_commitments.name: Nested governance
core_commitments.detail: Decisions are made at the smallest scale capable of responsibly holding the consequences.

core_commitments.name: Rights before efficiency
core_commitments.detail: Land access, privacy, cultural knowledge, Indigenous rights, youth safety, and affected-party consent cannot be overridden by a simple majority vote.

core_commitments.name: Projects before branding
core_commitments.detail: Trust is earned through visible usefulness, not claims or image alone.

core_commitments.name: Care, culture, ecology, and economy belong together
core_commitments.detail: They are treated as one operating system, not separate programs.

core_commitments.name: Monitoring must change decisions
core_commitments.detail: Every major project includes a baseline, target, review date, and adaptation rule.

core_commitments.name: AI assists but does not govern
core_commitments.detail: AI may help organize information, but it cannot decide legitimacy, rights, funding worthiness, truth, punishment, or who deserves care.

core_commitments.name: Knowledge should travel responsibly
core_commitments.detail: Methods are documented so other places can adapt them without copying or extracting local culture.

scales.work: Daily care, projects, learning, tools, food, mutual aid
Water, flooding, habitat, monitoring, cross-neighborhood work
Shared priorities, economy, education, media, and regional infrastructure
Peer learning, ecological comparison, seed and tool exchange

rule_of_scale: Organize daily work locally, water work by watershed, shared infrastructure and culture bioregionally, and ecological learning across the ecoregion.
atlas_layers: Food, energy, material, labor, money, and information flows
atlas_protection: Sensitive species locations, sacred places, cultural knowledge, private wells, personal information, and vulnerable residents must never be published without appropriate permission.
land_seat: Every council agenda includes a Land Seat: a steward who presents ecological observations, seasonal conditions, downstream effects, uncertainty, and red flags. The Land Seat does not claim to literally speak for nature; it ensures that more-than-human consequences are not omitted.
quest_override_rule: A high project score never overrides a red flag, missing consent, unsafe conditions, ecological harm, or the absence of a maintenance owner.
care_principle: Ecological work fails when people are exhausted, excluded, unpaid, unsafe, or unsupported. Care work, creative work, governance, ecological work, technical work, and learning are all recognized as real contributions.
credits_note: Credits should supplement fair wages, not disguise unpaid labour. Speculative tokens are not part of the minimum system. Greenfire Credits are designed as non-transferable internal contribution records — not cryptocurrency, legal tender, or an investment product.
ai_log_requirement: Whenever AI materially shapes a public report, map, plan, match, or recommendation, log the tool, purpose, data class, human reviewer, known limits, and correction path.

elder_guidance.headline: Indigenous Elders at the Forefront
elder_guidance.statement: Guidance is sought through relationships built on clear invitation, consent, compensation, cultural protocol, and continued accountability. Knowledge holders determine what may be recorded, shared, archived, commercialized, or kept private. Indigenous Elders are not decorative participants.
principles: Cultural boundaries set by Elders and their communities
The ability to withdraw or restrict material
Protection from unauthorized AI or data use
do_not: Do not state that all Indigenous people share one worldview
Do not imply an Elder speaks for an entire nation without confirmation
Do not claim tribal endorsement without written confirmation
Do not use Indigenous culture as marketing aesthetic
Do not record ceremonies or sacred knowledge automatically
Do not enter private or restricted knowledge into AI systems without documented consent

first_30_days: Form a founding team with distinct responsibilities
Identify Indigenous nations, watershed groups, community organizations, and existing institutions
Inventory skills, spaces, tools, and relationships
Publish a clear statement of what the chapter does and does not represent
by_90_days: Define roles, decision rights, privacy, conflict, youth, cultural, and data protocols
Establish a hub or host agreement
Choose and complete one visible, low-risk, maintainable project
Publish a public report and money summary
Name and prepare backups for critical roles
by_12_months: Establish youth learning and care systems
Publish a State of the Bioregion report
Review finances, access, conflicts, roles, and indicators
Release at least one reusable project toolkit

safety_limits: This framework is an organizational manual. It does not replace legal counsel, environmental engineering, ecological assessment, land-title review, permits and zoning review, insurance, youth safeguarding, public-health protocols, emergency management, or government-to-government and rights-holder consultation.
